chunks: As for him who is not in want of any thing,

key_terms.اسْتَغْنَى: became self-sufficient / was rich / was in no need

ai.seo_question: Who is the 'self-sufficient' person mentioned in Surah Abasa?
ai.summary: This segment from Surah Abasa refers to the wealthy or self-sufficient individual whom the Prophet (peace be upon him) initially turned away in favor of the blind companion, Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum. It highlights the ethical lesson that spiritual worth is not determined by worldly status or wealth. Shia exegetes, such as Allamah Tabatabai, emphasize that the divine rebuke was not a permanent rejection of the elite but a corrective measure to prevent the neglect of the humble, reinforcing the principle that sincerity of heart outweighs social prestige.
